steps.scene: You're in the left-hand lane when you realise the exit you wanted has just gone past.

options.text: Carry on to the next exit
Stop on the hard shoulder and reverse back carefully
Turn back through a gap in the central reservation

question.explanation: You must never reverse, cross the central reservation or drive against the traffic on a motorway.

steps.title: Plan your exit
steps.body: The first sign for an exit comes a mile before it, and another at half a mile. Get into the left-hand lane in good time.

question.prompt: Which lane should you be in well before your exit?

options.text: The middle lane
Any lane — you can cut across at the last moment
The left-hand lane

question.explanation: At 70 mph a mile goes by in under a minute. Move left early so you're never cutting across lanes.

question.prompt: Posts with three, then two, then one diagonal bar stand beside the left lane. What are they counting down to?

options.text: The next emergency telephone
The start of the exit slip road
A police speed check

question.explanation: Each bar is 100 yards: 300, 200, then 100 yards to the start of the slip road. By now you should already be in the left lane.

a.label: Limit in a red ring
a.body: Mandatory. At roadworks it's often enforced by cameras — slow down in good time.

b.label: Through the works
b.body: Keep your distance and stay in your lane. Workers and their vehicles may be close by.

question.prompt: What should you do when approaching roadworks on a motorway?

options.text: Speed up to get through the works quickly
Move onto the hard shoulder to get past
Keep to the lower speed limit

question.explanation: Lower limits at roadworks are the law, not a suggestion. Slow down before you reach them, not at the camera.

steps.scene: You're in a contraflow. Only a line of cones separates you from oncoming traffic, and the queue ahead keeps stopping.

options.text: Keep a good distance from the vehicle ahead
Stay close to the car in front to keep the queue short
Switch to whichever lane is moving faster

question.explanation: Lanes are narrow and there's no barrier to oncoming traffic. A good gap gives you room if the queue stops suddenly.

steps.scene: It's dark and pouring with rain on a three-lane motorway. You can see red studs on your left and white studs on your right.

options.text: The right-hand lane, next to the central reservation
The middle lane
The left-hand lane

question.explanation: Red studs mark the edge next to the hard shoulder; white ones divide the lanes. Red on your left means you're in the left lane.

steps.wrongBelief: You can stay in an outside lane until the countdown markers, then move across.

question.prompt: You're in the right-hand lane and pass the one-mile sign for your exit. What should you do?

options.text: Stay put until the countdown markers, then cut across
Start moving left in good time
Slow down in the right-hand lane until a gap appears

question.explanation: Cutting across lanes at the last moment forces others to brake. Work your way left one lane at a time, in good time.

steps.repairNote: Plan ahead: move into the left-hand lane well before the exit — the first sign is a mile out.
